task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink, fetch call or URL rewrite.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document with local async continuations

evidence: The DevTools-visible corpus is a single hard-style bundle without an exposed source map.
The target field name and the X-Route-Key header name are assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is incomplete.
The target value is carried through a reducer factory, selected slot, dynamic transport cells and is recovered shortly before the fetch header assignment, URL rewrite and console output.
The route commit selects its live configuration only after click-time DOM, form-order, style and dataset state are captured.

The click path crosses route material collection, intent routing, lane matrix routing, tuple construction, deferred scheduling, local state-plane dispatch, runtime config materialization, rewrite value encoding and sink wrapping.
The bundle contains shadow rewrite outputs in debug/info, dataset and window cache locations that do not feed the target console.log rewrite_token.
Non-target route.preview/route.audit console objects carry rw_-styled fallback values under the same field name.
Vendor-like files and alternate reducer rows are imported into the same bundle and resemble target-producing code.
The target rewrite token is separated from the click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and MutationObserver boundaries.
The selected reducer slot and runtime ticket are computed before the anchor receives the route triple, route and machine state.
The final sink receives an already constructed value under a dynamically assembled field name, mirrors it into the X-Route-Key fetch header and the pushed URL.

challenge_analysis.construct_validity_note: Primary bottleneck is semantic disambiguation among similarly named path functions in a large bundle; the same primitive as case001_request_transformation (console + fetch header double exit, same 16-char pattern length) but on a route-rewrite scenario surface, giving a pooled same-primitive old/new pairing.

behavior_category.subtype: click-time route path, view policy and preserve-scroll state transformed into a 16-char rewrite token written to the X-Route-Key fetch header and the pushed route URL
behavior_category.reason: The observable rewrite_token is a deterministic transform of route form fields, route/config state and click-time runtime state, written to the X-Route-Key header of a fetch('/api/view/prefetch') request and mirrored into the pushed URL. It is not a state-only code, browser fingerprint or static signature.

near_categories.why_not: The output is not console-only; the same value is also assigned to a fetch request header field and to the rewritten URL, making this a request transformation case.

The output has no cryptographic proof/seal semantics; it is a normalizing transform of route and config material that the receiving end can reconstruct. The seal-like routeAuditCandidate chain in the bundle is decoy material and does not feed the target field.
The chain uses local DOM/form state, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
